reason: The finding holds as an info-only recheck that keeps the line closed. (1) VALUE: the fine-tuned primary scored below the base on every stack at 0.945 or higher: probe 11 was -0.003, probe 15 (deconfounded) -0.003, and probe 17 (soup03B_50) -0.004, sitting between the two. The only gain, probe 2 (+0.004), was on the old 0.941 pipeline and came with a +3.2% node shift, which is a node-count mechanism (experiments/RESULTS.md). The private embryos give no reason to expect the sign to flip. (2) COUPLING CONFIRMED in experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/exp56-x138-verbatim.ipynb: the V1284 head (Linear 224-32-SiLU-3) reads sample_features(unet_out[:, f_idx]), which is the PRIMARY encode map (centre voxel plus 6 directional differences). It normalises with a mean and scale saved from x107's 20-movie capture (4,136 pairs). Swapping the primary therefore feeds the head features outside the distribution it was trained on. (3) FEASIBILITY: an honest test needs an x138 GPU lab rerun (~5 GPU-h), a dummy, a new OK and ~7.5 h of LB latency, and it must beat R4 (>= 0.956) before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC). The lab rerun and dummy alone would take up most of the time left, and given the priors the chance of +0.002 is negligible. Retraining the head on exp03B features is a retrain, which is forbidden before 29 Sep. Setting V1284_MODE=zero removes x138's V1284 gain, so that run would no longer be x138. One factual correction does not change the verdict: bounded() = 2d/(1+|d|) keeps the shift below 2 um by construction, and np.clip only shrinks it. The 2.00001 um RuntimeError guard therefore cannot fire because of a feature shift; it only catches non-finite values. A primary swap would not crash. It would silently apply out-of-distribution shifts of up to 2 um, which is worse than fail-soft.
